descriptionEn.after: The learner can distinguish absorbed dose, equivalent dose, and effective dose, determine the dose quantity appropriate to the question from given data under stated model assumptions, and assess the effectiveness of shielding by the reduction in dose under otherwise comparable exposure conditions.

atomicity.competenceCore: Quantitatively compare a shielding intervention using a correctly chosen and modeled dose quantity.
atomicity.rationale: Distinguishing the dose quantities and stating the applicable model are correctness conditions for the same calculation-and-interpretation task, not three independent assessment routines. The learner selects the quantity appropriate to the given problem; the wording does not require all three dose calculations in each task. One or two linked cases can assess the complete target.
atomicity.splitNotRequired: No compelling content split follows from the current dose-and-shielding target or these three clauses. Splitting into separate definition, arithmetic, and protection goals would artificially fragment this integrated application.

definitionsCheck.actuallyRead: Annex 18, B.1–2, official online text on 2026-09-07.
definitionsCheck.authorityLimit: Supplementary primary terminology check only, not a new curricular scope source, legal advice or a requirement to memorize regulatory tables.

doseDistinctions.meaning: Absorbed energy per mass; D = E_abs/m, measured in Gy. For tissue doses, the specified averaging region matters.

A radiation-quality-weighted dose quantity measured in Sv. Specify the convention and weighting factor in the model. In the organ-equivalent formulation H_T = sum_R w_R D_T,R; with one specified radiation component this reduces to w_R D_T. The SN quality-factor q notation is not asserted to be universally identical to every modern w_R or operational Q definition.

A protection quantity additionally combining weighted organ/tissue equivalent doses; E_eff = sum_T w_T H_T in the stated simplified organ model, measured in Sv. A single radiation-weighted absorbed dose is not automatically effective dose.

definitionsCheck.notationBoundary: E_abs denotes absorbed energy and E_eff effective dose here to avoid using E ambiguously. These explanatory equations belong to the proposal's correctness notes, not to an enlarged mandatory formula list in the goal.
definitionsCheck.riskBoundary: A dose-model comparison is not an individual clinical prognosis or a guarantee of safety.

taskModelConditions: State whether the given data represent absorbed energy/mass, a given tissue dose, or a given dose rate integrated over a specified duration.
Supply the relevant radiation/tissue weighting factors when needed; do not introduce a recall demand for entire regulatory tables.
For the shielding comparison keep incident source conditions, duration and geometry otherwise comparable, or quantify their stated differences explicitly.

Use an attenuation relation only within its stated radiation/material/energy and geometry assumptions. Do not assume a count-rate reduction universally equals an absorbed-, equivalent- or effective-dose reduction.

If shielding changes the radiation mixture or energy distribution, a simple unchanged-weight proportional reduction needs additional justification; a scalar-factor classroom model must state that simplification.
Criterion is the absolute or relative reduction in the same chosen dose quantity, not an unsupported assertion that any nonzero shielding eliminates risk.
A conceptual classification or a question asking what data are missing may demonstrate the distinction; not every case must numerically calculate all three quantities.
Use provided data or a simulation, not an invitation to unapproved exposure experiments.

assessmentBoundaryExample.status: Illustrative correctness control only; not a registered P evidence profile.
assessmentBoundaryExample.setup: In a supplied monoenergetic-photon model, the same 0.020 kg tissue region absorbs 4.0e-6 J without the shield and 1.0e-6 J with it over equal times and unchanged incident geometry. Set w_R = 1, and supply tissue weight w_T = 0.12; this modeled organ is the only nonzero organ contribution.
assessmentBoundaryExample.expected: D falls from 2.0e-4 Gy to 5.0e-5 Gy; H_T from 2.0e-4 Sv to 5.0e-5 Sv; the modeled contribution to effective dose falls from 2.4e-5 Sv to 6.0e-6 Sv. Each matched quantity is reduced by 75% under these explicit assumptions.
negativeControls: Equal numerical values of D and H_T when w_R=1 do not make their physical quantities or units interchangeable.
H_T alone is not effective dose; missing organ information generally prevents determining the full effective dose.
The stated 75% dose reduction is conditional on this model, not a universal shield property or evidence of zero hazard.
assessmentBoundaryExample.scope: A linked calculation and explanation tests the integrated core; these numerical constants and this particular organ are not additions to the canonical goal.
